features.note: Only two blades read clearly (middle light blade + darker lower blade); top blade is lost in shadow, and the two visible blades appear tilted the SAME direction (near-parallel), so opposed counter-rotation does not read at mid-travel.

Orange actuator body is present at correct side and plausible 163mm proportion, but it reads flush-mounted on the frame right face: no visible protruding shaft stub (>=37mm free spindle), no U-clamp, no anti-rotation strap — spec explicitly forbids flush mounting.

Black disc with white pointer is present on the actuator face (good blockout signal), but there is no 0-90 arc/dial plate block behind it; 1:1 rotation cannot be confirmed from a single still, judged on presence of pointer + arc blocking.
Frame reads as a channel with real depth and distinct flange plates on BOTH faces (front and rear flange planes clearly separated); proportions plausible for 600x400x127mm.

No crank or tie-rod blocking visible on the left (non-actuator) side; the camera azimuth partially occludes that side, but protruding cranks/tie rod would still catch the silhouette edge and none do. Score reflects what is observable; occlusion noted in defects.

important_features.note: No dark edge-strip blocking on blade meeting lines or jambs; judged leniently at blockout but nothing signals seals.
No plate block on the actuator face; printed text not expected at blockout, but a flat label-plate volume is absent.
Cable is present exiting the actuator underside, but it reads as a straight rigid rod at a fixed angle — no catenary droop.

defects: Top blade (blade_1) is not readable: the upper third of the opening is a dark shadowed region where a third blade should read distinctly.
The two visible blades appear tilted in the same direction (near-parallel), contradicting the opposed-blade identity ('never parallel mid-travel').
Actuator sits flush against the frame right face: no protruding drive-shaft stub, no visible free spindle gap, no U-clamp block, no anti-rotation strap block.
No crank-and-tie-rod linkage blocking on the non-actuator (left) side; camera azimuth 42deg also keeps that side mostly occluded, so it cannot be verified from this view.
Indicator is a bare disc + pointer with no 0-90 arc/dial plate behind it.
Cable exits as a straight rigid rod, not a drooping catenary.
No blocking for blade edge seals or actuator nameplate (lenient at blockout, recorded for the important_features average).
